Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview and Objective 2 Gameplay 3 End Game 4 Scoring Overview and Objective Board Game Arena game link: https://en.boardgamearena.com/#!gamepanel?game=veggiegarden In Veggie Garden, each player cultivates their vegetables to help the community garden prosper. A game plays out over 6 rounds, where each player takes turns manipulating the community garden to make it flourish. At the end of the game, each vegetable in the garden has a point value as shown by its associated fence post. Vegetables in the compost are worth zero points. Whoever has the most points wins. Gameplay One set of vegetables is removed from the game during setup, so that only 5 of the 6 veggies will be available in each game. On each player's turn, that player selects a face up card from the Harvest, places it in front of them, and takes the action associated with it on the reference tile. Actions will manipulate the community garden, and will usually affect the point values of the vegetables in the garden. Cabbage: Cabbage allows you to shift any one column or row of cards or fence posts. All cards/posts will either shift once place left, right, up or down. The Groundhog blocks the row and column he is part of. Carrots: Carrots allow you to choose any other fence post and swap it with the Bunny. At the end of the game, the card next to the Bunny does not earn any points. Peas: Whenever you harvest Peas, you may move the Groundhog to another space in the compost area, and select one other compost card adjacent to the Groundhog's new position (including the diagonal). Swap the selected card with the card on the Groundhog's direct opposite side. For example, if you chose the card to the Groundhog's lower left, then you would swap it with the card to the Groundhog's upper right. Peppers: Harvesting Peppers allows you to swap any two adjacent vegetable cards or fence posts vertically, horizontally or diagonally. The Groundhog blocks this vegetable. Potato: When you harvest a Potato, exchange a card from your hand with any one of the sixteen in the garden. The Groundhog blocks this vegetable. Tomato: When you harvest a Tomato, discard a vegetable from the garden and replace it with one of the remaining 3 from Harvest. The Groundhog blocks this vegetable. End Game When the last player has taken their last action and every player has 8 cards in their hand, beginning with the first player, each player takes one final card from the harvest. Cards are not replenished between picks and players do not take the associated actions. Scoring Veggies each score the sum of all their associated points in the garden as denoted by the fence posts. 10 bonus points are awarded to each player who has all five types of vegetables in the hand. community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] Somebody explain to me the point of publishing a game like this.  It is totally chaotic and there are plenty of other chaotic games. It is a filler and there are plenty of better fillers.  Like hundreds of games nowadays, it’s just “one more game around” and a few more logged trees.

[Rating: 1/10] Simple card drafting and movement, uninteresting after a while. Feels random and determined by the last drawn cards.

[Rating: 2/10] Fairly forgettable game with a charming setting in a communal garden. I didn't enjoy it enough to want to explore it further to see if it's as chaotic as trying to shape the garden and your hand at the same time felt.

[Rating: 2/10] It's a cute enough game. However, the decision making was somewhat basic and I feel like it really doesn't do enough to keep it from feeling pretty random in the end as to who will win. All the rounds and shuffling of items on the board only really delays everything until that last round when everything is decided.

[Rating: 3/10] This game was boring.  We were moving veggies all over the place, but in the end it is really only the last couple turns that matter since an action can really move lots of pieces around.  It makes it hard to be strategic.  Also, I wanted to like the theme (something other than orcs fighting zombies), but it just felt uninspiring.

[Rating: 3/10] Super swingy based on starting hand and board. It was quick and simple, but it was the first of their games that I've played that wasn't really fun.

[Rating: 3/10] Quick, simple and fun!?  Yeah right!  This game is kind of complicated for what it sells itself as, takes a looooooong half hour, and left everyone kind of saying, meh.

[Rating: 3/10] I won this game without knowing the rules and making random moves. Looks like it's too random to be fun.

[Rating: 3/10] [i]Draft and maneuver vegetables in this game of garden variety.[/i] Played in: [url=https://boardgamegeek.com/geeklist/310808/item/10179927][u]2023[/u][/url]

[Rating: 4/10] I had high hopes for this as a great 2 player game for my wife and I.  Rating is based on 2 player game only.  I'll have to reavaluate when I play with more.
